title: ETH versus Gap-ETH
formal: Does the deterministic Exponential Time Hypothesis imply the deterministic Gap Exponential Time Hypothesis for sparse 3-CNF formulas?
definitions: For a 3-CNF formula F with n variables, let \(\operatorname{val}(F)\) be the maximum fraction of clauses simultaneously satisfiable. The ETH convention here asserts that there is \(c>0\) for which no deterministic algorithm decides satisfiability of all 3-CNF formulas in time \(O(2^{cn} \operatorname{poly}(\mathrm{L}))\), where L is the binary encoding length. Gap-ETH asserts that there exist constants \(B\ge 1, \delta \in (0,1)\) and \(c' >0\) for which no deterministic algorithm in time \(O(2^{c' n} \operatorname{poly}(\mathrm{L}))\) distinguishes \(\operatorname{val}(F)=1\) from \(\operatorname{val}(F)\le 1- \delta\) on formulas with at most Bn clauses. Its inputs are promised to satisfy one of those two alternatives. Empty formulas are satisfiable. All constants are fixed independently of F; randomized versions are not asserted.

context_blocks.text: ETH concerns exact satisfiability, while Gap-ETH postulates comparable exponential hardness even when unsatisfiable inputs violate a fixed fraction of clauses. Their equivalence would unify many exact and approximation lower-bound assumptions.

Bitansky and coauthors distinguish ETH from the stronger gap hypothesis while obtaining exponential hardness for particular approximation tasks. Hardness for those tasks does not imply a gap-preserving sparse 3-CNF statement. This implication is distinct from asking whether either hypothesis is true.

why: Clarify whether a major approximation-hardness assumption adds strength to the standard exact exponential-time hypothesis.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
